% Shared Tikz Preamble for Diagram Atomization Pipeline
% Load this in every tikz generated by Phase 5 subagents.
% Do NOT redefine these — use exactly this preamble.

\documentclass[tikz,border=2pt]{standalone}

% Core libraries
\usetikzlibrary{
    arrows.meta,       % arrow styles
    positioning,       % relative placement
    cd,                % commutative diagrams (tikz-cd)
    calc,              % coordinate calculations
    shapes.geometric,  % ellipses, polygons, etc.
    shapes.misc,       % rounded rectangles, etc.
    decorations.markings,  % arrow on paths
    backgrounds,       % background layer
    fit,               % fitting nodes around others
}

% Standard arrow tip
\tikzset{>=Stealth}

% Commutative diagram style
\tikzcdset{
    arrows={>=Stealth},
    row sep/normal=3em,
    column sep/normal=4em,
}

% Common node styles
\tikzset{
    mathnode/.style={rectangle, draw=none, fill=none, inner sep=2pt},
    labelnode/.style={rectangle, draw=none, fill=none, font=\small, inner sep=1pt},
}

\begin{document}
% Subagents: put your tikz code here.
% Use tikzcd for commutative diagrams, tikzpicture for others.
% Keep it self-contained — the \end{document} is at bottom.
%
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
% 3D strongly convex cone sigma in N_R = R^3
% Three rays: rho1 (x+), rho2 (y+), rho3 (z+)
% Red shading fills cone interior (visible triangular face)
% Coordinate axes with tick marks; origin labeled "0"
% Perspective: looking down from above the first octant
% ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

\usetikzlibrary{3d}

\begin{tikzpicture}[
    x={(3.0cm, 1.2cm)},
    y={(2.0cm, -1.5cm)},
    z={(0cm, 3.0cm)},
    >=Stealth,
    line cap=round,
    line join=round,
]

% Cone extent (max coordinate value)
\def\L{4}

% ── AXES WITH TICK MARKS ──

% X-axis: positive (dashed black), negative (solid green)
% Positive side
\draw[dashed, black, thick] (0,0,0) -- (\L+0.8,0,0);
\draw[->, dashed, black, thick] (\L+0.4,0,0) -- (\L+0.8,0,0);
% Negative side
\draw[green!60!black, thick] (0,0,0) -- (-\L-0.5,0,0);
\draw[->, green!60!black, thick] (-\L-0.3,0,0) -- (-\L-0.5,0,0);

% X tick marks: -25,-20,...,30 (scaled: /5 so -5..6)
\foreach \t in {-5,-4,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4,5,6}{
    \pgfmathsetmacro{\tx}{\t * 0.8}
    \draw[black, thin] (\tx, 0.12, 0) -- (\tx, -0.12, 0);
}

% Y-axis: solid red (both directions)
\draw[red, thick] (0,-\L-0.5,0) -- (0,\L+0.8,0);
\draw[->, red, thick] (0,\L+0.4,0) -- (0,\L+0.8,0);
\draw[->, red, thick] (0,-\L-0.3,0) -- (0,-\L-0.5,0);

% Y tick marks: -20,-15,...,30 (scaled: /5 so -4..6)
\foreach \t in {-4,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4,5,6}{
    \pgfmathsetmacro{\ty}{\t * 0.8}
    \draw[black, thin] (0.12, \ty, 0) -- (-0.12, \ty, 0);
}

% Z-axis: positive solid blue, negative dashed blue
\draw[blue, thick] (0,0,0) -- (0,0,\L+0.8);
\draw[->, blue, thick] (0,0,\L+0.4) -- (0,0,\L+0.8);
\draw[blue, dashed, thick] (0,0,0) -- (0,0,-\L-0.5);
\draw[->, blue, dashed, thick] (0,0,-\L-0.3) -- (0,0,-\L-0.5);

% Z tick marks: -10,-5,0,5,10 (scaled: /5 so -2..2)
\foreach \t in {-2,-1,1,2}{
    \pgfmathsetmacro{\tz}{\t * 0.8}
    \draw[black, thin] (0.08, 0, \tz) -- (-0.08, 0, \tz);
}

% ── REFERENCE PLANES ──

% Grey horizontal plane (xy-plane, z=0) — semi-transparent
\fill[gray!30, opacity=0.35]
    (-\L-0.5, -\L-0.5, 0) --
    (\L+0.8, -\L-0.5, 0) --
    (\L+0.8, \L+0.8, 0) --
    (-\L-0.5, \L+0.8, 0) -- cycle;
\draw[gray!50, thin] (-\L-0.5, -\L-0.5, 0) -- (\L+0.8, -\L-0.5, 0)
                     -- (\L+0.8, \L+0.8, 0) -- (-\L-0.5, \L+0.8, 0) -- cycle;

% Reddish vertical plane (xz-plane, y=0) — semi-transparent
\fill[red!25, opacity=0.35]
    (-\L-0.5, 0, -\L-0.5) --
    (\L+0.8, 0, -\L-0.5) --
    (\L+0.8, 0, \L+0.8) --
    (-\L-0.5, 0, \L+0.8) -- cycle;
\draw[red!40, thin] (-\L-0.5, 0, -\L-0.5) -- (\L+0.8, 0, -\L-0.5)
                     -- (\L+0.8, 0, \L+0.8) -- (-\L-0.5, 0, \L+0.8) -- cycle;

% ── CONE (red shading for the strongly convex cone sigma) ──
% The cone sigma = cone(e1, e2, e3) in the first octant
% Its intersection with the plane x+y+z=4 is a triangular face

% Draw the 3 cone rays (generators) — these are the positive coordinate directions
% rho_x+ : (1,0,0) direction — dashed black (consistent with canonical)
\draw[->, dashed, black, very thick] (0,0,0) -- (\L, 0, 0);
% rho_y+ : (0,1,0) direction — solid red
\draw[->, red, very thick] (0,0,0) -- (0, \L, 0);
% rho_z+ : (0,0,1) direction — solid blue
\draw[->, blue, very thick] (0,0,0) -- (0, 0, \L);

% Fill the cone interior (visible triangular face at x+y+z = \L)
% This is the intersection of the cone with the plane x+y+z = \L
\fill[red, opacity=0.35]
    (\L, 0, 0) -- (0, \L, 0) -- (0, 0, \L) -- cycle;

% Outline of the cone's triangular face
\draw[red!80!black, thick] (\L, 0, 0) -- (0, \L, 0) -- (0, 0, \L) -- cycle;

% Subtle edge lines from origin to the triangle vertices (cone generators)
% Already drawn above as the 3 rays, but draw them again on top for clarity
\draw[->, dashed, black, very thick] (0,0,0) -- (\L, 0, 0);
\draw[->, red, very thick] (0,0,0) -- (0, \L, 0);
\draw[->, blue, very thick] (0,0,0) -- (0, 0, \L);

% ── TICK LABELS ──
% Note: scaled coordinates; real tick values shown
% X-axis labels (reduced set for readability)
\foreach \t/\val in {-5/-25, -4/-20, -3/-15, -2/-10, -1/-5, 1/5, 2/10, 3/15, 4/20, 5/25, 6/30}{
    \pgfmathsetmacro{\tx}{\t * 0.8}
    \node[anchor=north, font=\tiny, inner sep=1pt] at (\tx, -0.2, 0) {\val};
}

% Y-axis labels (reduced set)
\foreach \t/\val in {-4/-20, -3/-15, -2/-10, -1/-5, 1/5, 2/10, 3/15, 4/20, 5/25, 6/30}{
    \pgfmathsetmacro{\ty}{\t * 0.8}
    \node[anchor=east, font=\tiny, inner sep=1pt] at (-0.25, \ty, 0) {\val};
}

% Z-axis labels
\foreach \t/\val in {-2/-10, -1/-5, 1/5, 2/10}{
    \pgfmathsetmacro{\tz}{\t * 0.8}
    \node[anchor=south east, font=\tiny, inner sep=1pt] at (-0.1, 0, \tz) {\val};
}

% Origin label
\node[anchor=north east, font=\small] at (0,0,0) {$0$};

% ── AXIS LABELS ──
% (per canonical: "none (numeric tick marks only; no x/y/z labels)" — but adding
%  small axis indicators for orientation, matching typical mathematical diagrams)
\node[anchor=south west, font=\small] at (\L+0.8, 0, 0) {$x$};
\node[anchor=south east, font=\small] at (0, \L+0.8, 0) {$y$};
\node[anchor=south, font=\small] at (0, 0, \L+0.8) {$z$};

\end{tikzpicture}

\end{document}
